agents.note: SPRINT 63 (V0.29.17) COMPLETE -- 4/4 (US-488, US-489, US-490, US-491). US-491 DONE (passes:true) 4/4 -- Iris polish P-3, DTC detail overlay hierarchy. THE FINDING IS THE STORY, and it is the most important thing to carry forward: `detailLine()` wraps EVERY row's text in a `.detail-value` span, and that span declared its OWN `font-size: 13px; color: var(--text-primary)`. A CHILD'S OWN DECLARATION BEATS AN INHERITED VALUE NO MATTER HOW SPECIFIC THE PARENT SELECTOR IS -- so US-488's entire tier ramp on `.detail-directive`, built one story ago, tested and shipped, PAINTED NOTHING: a STOP directive rendered identical to a MINOR one. Same for the amber caveat, the muted footer/meta and `.dtc-fix-directive`. GENERALIZABLE LESSON: a CSS test that asserts a PARENT rule's declaration proves the declaration EXISTS, never that it reaches the glyphs. If the text lives in a child with its own rule, the parent loses and the test passes anyway. My guard asserts the CHILD inherits -- the only form that catches this. AC-1: band leads (ordering asserted on the real DOM builder), 18px/800 padded slab with a `currentColor` left edge so the tier rules keep setting exactly ONE property and the accent can never disagree with the text beside it; guard demands a FULL STEP above base copy, not a token 1px bump. SECOND JUDGEMENT CALL: AC-1's parenthetical says green 'keeps' SAFE TO CLEAR ONCE LOGGED -- it never rendered. `codeDetailView` gated the band on isStopWatch, so MINOR and uncurated codes got NO band while the takeover has shown both since US-405 and US-488 had already shipped (dead) CSS for both tiers. On the ONE screen you open to ask 'what do I do', a blank answer reads as 'nothing to worry about' -- the dishonest answer on an uncurated code (F-1). Band now renders for every actionable tier; `na` ALONE stays blank (a fact, not an instruction; never alarms anywhere else; the fix slot already says it) -- pinned by my guard AND the pre-existing deploy-kit assertion. AC-2: one shared `.detail-card` shell across freeze/fix/Clear; the fix card's label was BRANCH-LOCAL inside `mode==='fix'`, so a STOP/WATCH card rendered a bordered box with NO heading -- now unconditional via a new `fixSectionLabel(mode)` export, mode-driven because heading a diagnose directive 'SUGGESTED FIX' would undo S-4 in the label while the body still obeys it. AC-3: `.detail-head` was a FIXED 36px around a 40px Back target -- the control that guarantees you are never trapped overflowed its own header; min-height 44px now, plus a real border (40px of transparent nothing is not a target you can see). AC-4 asserted, not assured: 5 re-run guards cover S-4, the trust badge, all 5 clear-gate reasons, the chip/tier table and the stop/watch wording. WALKED INTO THE US-490 TRAP FOR REAL: the card shell gave #dtc-clear-zone `display:flex`, which OUTRANKS the UA [hidden] rule -- hiding it would have painted an empty labelled box anyway. Stated `#dtc-clear-zone[hidden]{display:none}` explicitly, with a guard. Two of my own guards also pointed at strings the refactor moved and one regex window could have run past its branch onto the OLD label -- re-bounded by index slicing, watched red first.
